tools.name: publish_site
tools.description: Use this when the user wants something put online, shared as a link, or hosted. Publishes files to a live permanent URL at the chosen slug. Paths are stored exactly. Returns {url, path_url, slug, version, token?}. On deed.page, url and path_url are both https://{slug}.deed.page/. The token appears o

tools.name: update_site
tools.description: Use this to replace (or with merge=true, add to) the files of a slug you already own. Requires the token from the first publish. To undo, call restore_version. Returns the same shape as publish_site with a bumped version. Pass expected_version (the live vN) so a stale write returns version_conflict

tools.name: get_site
tools.description: Use this to check whether a slug is live and read its URL, version, size, and timestamps. Public; no token needed.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: Use this to list every live site owned by your token, with URLs and versions.

tools.name: delete_site
tools.description: Use this only when the user explicitly asks to take a site down. Permanently removes the slug you own and detaches its custom hostnames. The slug becomes free.

tools.name: rotate_token
tools.description: Use this after a leak, or to retire a token an agent should stop using. Issues a new token for the same principal. Every site carries over. The previous token stops working immediately unless overlap_seconds is set (0 to 300). During that window both tokens work. After it, the previous token returns

tools.name: revoke_token
tools.description: Use this when a token has leaked and you do not want a replacement yet. scope "current" (default) revokes the token you sent. scope "all" revokes every token for that principal, including any overlap window. A later call with a revoked token returns 401 token_revoked, not 403 suspended. Sites stay o

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Use this to read your plan, limits, how many sites your token owns, and how many custom hostnames it has attached.

tools.name: get_upgrade_link
tools.description: Use this only when the user asks for higher limits. Returns a Stripe Checkout URL for Hobby ($3/mo) or Pro ($15/mo) tied to your token. A human must open it and pay; nothing is charged by this call.

tools.name: list_versions
tools.description: Use this to see every retained version of a slug you own, newest first. Each entry has version, created_at, file_count, bytes, kind (publish, merge, or restore), restored_from, and a public permalink. Free keeps 10, Hobby 50, Pro unlimited.

tools.name: restore_version
tools.description: Use this to undo a publish. Creates a new version whose files equal the retained version, without re-uploading. Pass expected_version (the live vN). A mismatch returns version_conflict and does not write. The old permalink keeps serving until retention drops it.

tools.name: add_domain
tools.description: Use this when the user wants their own hostname on a site they own. Adds the hostname to the project and returns dns_records to create: a CNAME for a subdomain, an A record or an ALIAS record for an apex (create one, not both), and every TXT record. Status starts at pending_dns until DNS and the cer

tools.name: list_domains
tools.description: Use this to list custom hostnames on one slug, or on every site your token owns when slug is omitted. Status is the last checked value. Call domain_status to refresh it.

tools.name: remove_domain
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a hostname detached. Removes it from the project so requests to that host no longer serve the site.

tools.name: domain_status
tools.description: Use this after add_domain, once DNS might have propagated. Refreshes verification, DNS config, and certificate state. status is pending_dns, verifying, issuing_cert, active, or error. dns_records are the records to create. An error includes the reason.

tools.name: plan_upload
tools.description: Use this when the site is larger than about 4 MB, or when you already know each file's sha256. Send a manifest of {path, sha256, size, content_type?}. Returns which hashes are already stored and a direct upload URL for each missing hash. Upload those bytes, then call finalize_upload with the session

tools.name: finalize_upload
tools.description: Use this after plan_upload, once every missing blob has been uploaded. Checks hashes, screens the new bytes, and commits one version under the slug lock. A stale expected version returns version_conflict and writes nothing. A bad hash returns hash_mismatch. An expired session returns session_expired

tools.name: get_manifest
tools.description: Public. Returns the canonical manifest (paths, sha256, sizes, version, slug, created_at) and an Ed25519 signature, or signature null when the server has no signing key. Omit version for the live site. Verify with the keys at /.well-known/deed-signing-keys.json, then hash the files served at site_url

tools.name: site_analytics
tools.description: Owner-only cookieless counts for a slug: views per UTC day, top paths, top referrer hosts, and AI crawler counts by user-agent family. from and to are YYYY-MM-DD (default last 7 days, max 90). The accuracy field describes under-counting. No raw IP or full user agent is stored.

tools.name: set_site_access
tools.description: Hobby and Pro only. Sets a password (8 to 200 characters) or clears it when password is null. The hash is scrypt. Visitors get a host-only HttpOnly Secure cookie. Version permalinks and custom domains of the site are gated too. Free returns plan_required. Clearing is allowed on every plan.

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.description: Registers an http(s) URL for site.published, site.version_restored, site.deleted, site.taken_down, domain.active, and report.received. The HMAC secret is returned once. Free 1, Hobby 5, Pro 20. Private, internal, and localhost targets are rejected. Delivery is best-effort: 3 attempts, then stop.

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: Lists webhook URLs for your token. Secrets are not included.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Deletes one webhook by id from list_webhooks or create_webhook.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_site, list_sites, get_upgrade_link, list_webhooks · Private data: publish_site, update_site, get_site, list_sites, rotate_token, revoke_token, whoami, get_upgrade_link, restore_version, add_domain, list_domains, domain_status, plan_upload, get_manifest, set_site_access, create_webhook, list_webhooks · Public sink: publish_site, update_site, revoke_token, list_versions, restore_version, plan_upload, finalize_upload, create_webhook, list_webhooks, delete_webhook · Destructive: delete_site, remove_domain, delete_webhook.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_site, list_sites, get_upgrade_link, list_webhooks · Private data: publish_site, update_site, get_site, list_sites, rotate_token, revoke_token, whoami, get_upgrade_link, restore_version, add_domain, list_domains, domain_status, plan_upload, get_manifest, set_site_access, create_webhook, list_webhooks · Public sink: publish_site, update_site, revoke_token, list_versions, restore_version, plan_upload, finalize_upload, create_webhook, list_webhooks, delete_webhook · Destructive: delete_site, remove_domain, delete_webhook

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "publish_site" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
